npc.barkeep.flavor_text: I hear things. Rumors, contracts, the names of folk in trouble. Ask around.
npc.guild_master.flavor_text: Trade routes open, trade routes close. Coin flows. Mind the tariffs.
npc.militia_captain.flavor_text: Order above all. Walk the beat, report what you see, and keep your weapon sheathed until it isn't.
npc.research_officer.flavor_text: We got some new tech coming soon. Just need a bit more time in quality assurance. It's going to change the universe.
step.prologue_mars_entrance.description: The martian rock merges with high tech metal machinery. You see a wall that undulates before you as you examine it. An alien console stands before it, still with power. But a mystery you can't solve alone.
step.prologue_mars_entrance.title: The Door
step.prologue_mars_unlocked.description: The coordinates point to a remote stretch of Mars beyond the settlements. Something could be there. Worth taking a look at least.
step.prologue_mars_unlocked.title: Mars
step.prologue_seek_help.description: Nothing you try on your own is working. Ask around for help. The Merchants have connections. The Bar knows secrets. The Militia has records. The Labs would die to get their hands on alien tech.
step.prologue_seek_help.dialogue.barkeep: Then we have an understanding. I will send you to the old hand. Do not ask him what was behind the door until he decides you are ready to hear it. If you come back, the bar will keep your glass full while you tell the story.

Heard about the thing in the dust? Then you heard the wrong story. The militia calls it a sealed site. The old routes call it a door that took a hand and gave nothing back. One man got close to opening it. He has spent the years since pretending he never did. I can put you in the same room with him.
You chose another road in. Fine. Just remember that official reports are written by the people who survive them. If you come back, tell the bar what the reports leave out.
step.prologue_seek_help.dialogue.guild_m: The contract is filed. Build the cutter, open the door, and bring us something no one else can value yet. That is where the best margins begin.

Alien infrastructure on Mars is not a curiosity. It is an asset with no owner, no patent, and no surviving claimant. Sign the contract and the Guild will put a cutter in your hands that can read the door's material stress. First rights to whatever is recovered. We can decide what it is worth after we know how much of the future it contains.
Another party is funding the operation. An unfortunate choice, but not an irreversible one. If you recover anything the Guild can refine, transport, or sell, our office remains open.
step.prologue_seek_help.dialogue.militia: The paperwork is moving. When the package is ready, you will hear from me through a channel that officially does not exist. Until then, forget the coordinates.

There is no door. That is the official answer, and you will repeat it if anyone asks. ...Off the books: a patrol found the same material during the Incident. We lost people, buried the report, and learned that some doors are built to keep something in. I can give you a breach package. You can give me one thing in return: silence until we know what we are dealing with.
You chose another sponsor. Then keep the operation away from the patrol. We have enough old mistakes on the books already.
step.prologue_seek_help.dialogue.researc: We got some new tech coming soon. Just need a bit more time in quality assurance. It's going to change the universe.
A structure this old should not be receiving transmissions. We need more data. Attach this device to the console. It'll record what it can find. Bring it back here and we'll figure this puzzle out.
You found another method. If you recover evidence, send it to the station. We will study it before we decide whether it is a warning, a weapon, or something that has no human category.
step.prologue_seek_help.dialogue.xenolin: Then the work begins. Take a controlled sample from Mars and bring it back. We will publish the evidence when we know what it means, not before. The difference may keep people alive.

The signal is not a message in any human sense. It is a pattern with coordinates embedded inside it, and the door may be made of the same impossible material. Bring me a sample. We may be able to make the lock answer without teaching ourselves what it was built to contain.
You found another method. If you recover evidence, send it to the station. We will study it before we decide whether it is a warning, a weapon, or something that has no human category.
step.prologue_seek_help.title: Seek Help
step.prologue_signal.title: The Signal
